    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<p>I'm playing the PC game <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/803050/Per_Aspera/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Per Aspera</a> with Steam, and attempting to edit a save. When I opened a <code>.save</code> file in the SaveGames folder with Notepad++, the text had some recognizable words, but most of it is random unknown characters.</p>
<p>Below is a sample of the text, and an image of what it looks like in Notepad++. The file has over 26,000 lines.</p>
<p>I'm assuming the file is using some encoding I'm not familiar with, or needs to be opened in a program other than Notepad++. How can I open this file so it's readable by a human and I can make edits?</p>
<p>Lines 9-12. All <code>code blocks</code> are a single character in Notepad++</p>
<blockquote>
<p>{9} ÄúÅ <code>NAK</code> y÷ <code>DLE</code> E <code>DC2</code> <code>SI</code><br/>
{10} øöéÄ <code>NAK</code> Ã´ <code>ENQ</code> E <code>GS</code> IÓæÄ <code>SUB</code> <code>DC1</code><br/>
{11} <code>SI</code> resource_crater% <code>NUL</code> <code>NUL</code> €?5×£dB@ <code>NUL</code> H <code>NUL</code> P <code>NUL</code> X <code>SOH</code> <code>NUL</code> mZ <code>NUL</code> <code>DLE</code> 1Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>ETX</code> Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>ETX</code> Q <code>NUL</code> €.ƒMÅ <code>NAK</code> “[ Q <code>NUL</code> ïR ¿D <code>NAK</code> _†ÿD <code>GS</code> <code>GB</code> J <code>VT</code> ÅQ <code>NUL</code> <code>ACK</code> 0\jQ <code>NUL</code> <code>FS</code> <code>SOH</code> Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>EOT</code> Q <code>NUL</code> ÿ<br/>
{12} &lt;G%Ä <code>NAK</code> RQùD <code>DC2</code> <code>SI</code></p>
</blockquote>

<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">If you wanted to edit a specific in-game value (like how much money you have), you could potentially open it with a hex editor, look for that value in various formats, cross-reference that with a save with a different value to eliminate duplicates, and then just change it (but back it up first). That's basically the same approach one can use to edit the values in-memory for a running game. But that isn't guaranteed to work and requires a decent amount of advanced computing knowledge to do.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<span class="comment-copy">I don't think you understand just how much work could be involved in answering this question fully (except by one of the game developers). If you want a peek into what it takes, a good search term is "reverse engineering". <a href="https://www.muppetlabs.com/~breadbox/txt/bure.html" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Here's</a> a very entertaining post reverse engineering a very simple (!) format for a game from the 80's that should give you a bit of an idea how much more work it is to even <i>know</i> the answer than it is to write the answer.</span>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h3>Short answer:</h3>
<p>You can edit the file using a "hex editor", but you can't make it human-readable.</p>
<h3>Long answer:</h3>
<p>This is a binary file. It means that every byte in that file is supposed to be interpreted as a byte, as opposed to a human-readable character. For example, the first 15 characters in the first line in your screenshot:</p>
<pre><code>NUL NUL NUL BS NUL DLE   SUB ENQ 2 9 6 5 8 8
</code></pre>
<p>represent the following 15 values:</p>
<pre><code>0 0 0 8 0 16 32 26 5 50 57 54 53 56 56
</code></pre>
<p>Notepad++ is interpreting those values as if they represented text. But since this isn't a text file, you only get gibberish. The readable words, on the other hand, are actual text embedded within the file.</p>
<p>Binary files are typically edited in what is known as a "hex editor". It's the only way to write values that represent non-printable characters, such as any value below 32 (whitespace), among others. Unfortunately, a hex editor won't make the file any more readable. Nothing will. After all, what does the first <code>0</code> in the above example stand for? Do the first 4 values together represent a single 32 bit integer? Or do they form a 32 bit float? No general-purpose software can tell you that, much less what it'll affect in the game.</p>
<p>You will need to either gain access to the game's code, or reverse engineer it, if you want to make sense of this file. If you can't do either, you'll have to wait for someone else to do it and release a save editor for this game.</p>
<p>Note that you should always keep a backup of the save file before attempting any edits yourself. Some games may include some form of integrity check (such as a hash) to check for tampering (cheating) or file corruption (e.g. incomplete save due to unexpected crash), or you may accidentally enter an invalid value, causing the game to flag the file as corrupt.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is a binary or encoded file.</p>
<p>Basically, it's written in a way that only something that has a decoder for that specific format will be able to read. Really, I'm surprised that there are a few readable words in there.</p>
<p>Try opening an image with Notepad++, it will look not far off. And its just that image showing programs know how to take that mess and figure out an image out of it.</p>
<p>So except if someone developed a save file editor for the game you are currently playing, there is no way to humanly modify that file. If you change even 1 letter of this mess, your save file will be lost.</p>
<p>But why is it like that? Well, my guess is that developers usually don't like you editing the file and giving you weird, probably untested states of the game. But that is not much more than a guess on my part.</p>
</div>

<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">"compiled" is the wrong word here. Generally you'd say it's "encoded in a binary format", where "binary" just means an arbitrary, non-text encoding.</span>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">The simplest way to write data to a file is actually to <i>not</i> make it human-readable: you just directly dump some object in memory to file. Making it human-readable requires a bit more work, making it human-editable requires even more work (since you need to verify the data being read in), and it makes the file a bit bigger (but that part is usually negligible for save files, given how small they are). It isn't part of the intended gaming experience for people to edit their save files, so there's little reason to provide this functionality.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">@TimmyJim Many of the readable strings in binary files would be there because that's just part of whatever binary data they wanted to store (or because it's noise). If you dump some amount of numbers and some amount of strings to file, those would just all be squashed together, the numbers would be gibberish, while the strings may already be in a format that text editors can display.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">@murgatroid99 Dumping <i>an entire section of memory</i> might well not be possible, but it's far easier to save and load the memory representation of an integer, or even a variable-length list of integers, than to convert it into an equivalent text representation. Most binary file formats don't have a formal "serialization scheme", just ad hoc instructions for how to pack and unpack a stream of bytes, as in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-doc/26fb6c06-4e5c-4778-ab4e-edbf26a545bb" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this documentation of part of the legacy Microsoft Word format</a>.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I'm playing the PC game <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/803050/Per_Aspera/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Per Aspera</a> with Steam, and attempting to edit a save. When I opened a <code>.save</code> file in the SaveGames folder with Notepad++, the text had some recognizable words, but most of it is random unknown characters.</p>
<p>Below is a sample of the text, and an image of what it looks like in Notepad++. The file has over 26,000 lines.</p>
<p>I'm assuming the file is using some encoding I'm not familiar with, or needs to be opened in a program other than Notepad++. How can I open this file so it's readable by a human and I can make edits?</p>
<p>Lines 9-12. All <code>code blocks</code> are a single character in Notepad++</p>
<blockquote>
<p>{9} ÄúÅ <code>NAK</code> y÷ <code>DLE</code> E <code>DC2</code> <code>SI</code><br/>
{10} øöéÄ <code>NAK</code> Ã´ <code>ENQ</code> E <code>GS</code> IÓæÄ <code>SUB</code> <code>DC1</code><br/>
{11} <code>SI</code> resource_crater% <code>NUL</code> <code>NUL</code> €?5×£dB@ <code>NUL</code> H <code>NUL</code> P <code>NUL</code> X <code>SOH</code> <code>NUL</code> mZ <code>NUL</code> <code>DLE</code> 1Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>ETX</code> Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>ETX</code> Q <code>NUL</code> €.ƒMÅ <code>NAK</code> “[ Q <code>NUL</code> ïR ¿D <code>NAK</code> _†ÿD <code>GS</code> <code>GB</code> J <code>VT</code> ÅQ <code>NUL</code> <code>ACK</code> 0\jQ <code>NUL</code> <code>FS</code> <code>SOH</code> Q <code>NUL</code> <code>DC1</code> <code>EOT</code> Q <code>NUL</code> ÿ<br/>
{12} &lt;G%Ä <code>NAK</code> RQùD <code>DC2</code> <code>SI</code></p>
</blockquote>

<span class="comment-copy">If you wanted to edit a specific in-game value (like how much money you have), you could potentially open it with a hex editor, look for that value in various formats, cross-reference that with a save with a different value to eliminate duplicates, and then just change it (but back it up first). That's basically the same approach one can use to edit the values in-memory for a running game. But that isn't guaranteed to work and requires a decent amount of advanced computing knowledge to do.</span>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<h3>Short answer:</h3>
<p>You can edit the file using a "hex editor", but you can't make it human-readable.</p>
<h3>Long answer:</h3>
<p>This is a binary file. It means that every byte in that file is supposed to be interpreted as a byte, as opposed to a human-readable character. For example, the first 15 characters in the first line in your screenshot:</p>
<pre><code>NUL NUL NUL BS NUL DLE   SUB ENQ 2 9 6 5 8 8
</code></pre>
<p>represent the following 15 values:</p>
<pre><code>0 0 0 8 0 16 32 26 5 50 57 54 53 56 56
</code></pre>
<p>Notepad++ is interpreting those values as if they represented text. But since this isn't a text file, you only get gibberish. The readable words, on the other hand, are actual text embedded within the file.</p>
<p>Binary files are typically edited in what is known as a "hex editor". It's the only way to write values that represent non-printable characters, such as any value below 32 (whitespace), among others. Unfortunately, a hex editor won't make the file any more readable. Nothing will. After all, what does the first <code>0</code> in the above example stand for? Do the first 4 values together represent a single 32 bit integer? Or do they form a 32 bit float? No general-purpose software can tell you that, much less what it'll affect in the game.</p>
<p>You will need to either gain access to the game's code, or reverse engineer it, if you want to make sense of this file. If you can't do either, you'll have to wait for someone else to do it and release a save editor for this game.</p>
<p>Note that you should always keep a backup of the save file before attempting any edits yourself. Some games may include some form of integrity check (such as a hash) to check for tampering (cheating) or file corruption (e.g. incomplete save due to unexpected crash), or you may accidentally enter an invalid value, causing the game to flag the file as corrupt.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is a binary or encoded file.</p>
<p>Basically, it's written in a way that only something that has a decoder for that specific format will be able to read. Really, I'm surprised that there are a few readable words in there.</p>
<p>Try opening an image with Notepad++, it will look not far off. And its just that image showing programs know how to take that mess and figure out an image out of it.</p>
<p>So except if someone developed a save file editor for the game you are currently playing, there is no way to humanly modify that file. If you change even 1 letter of this mess, your save file will be lost.</p>
<p>But why is it like that? Well, my guess is that developers usually don't like you editing the file and giving you weird, probably untested states of the game. But that is not much more than a guess on my part.</p>
</div>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">The simplest way to write data to a file is actually to <i>not</i> make it human-readable: you just directly dump some object in memory to file. Making it human-readable requires a bit more work, making it human-editable requires even more work (since you need to verify the data being read in), and it makes the file a bit bigger (but that part is usually negligible for save files, given how small they are). It isn't part of the intended gaming experience for people to edit their save files, so there's little reason to provide this functionality.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">
– <a class="comment-user" href="/users/49119/notthatguy" title="357 reputation">NotThatGuy</a>

<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">@TimmyJim Many of the readable strings in binary files would be there because that's just part of whatever binary data they wanted to store (or because it's noise). If you dump some amount of numbers and some amount of strings to file, those would just all be squashed together, the numbers would be gibberish, while the strings may already be in a format that text editors can display.</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">@murgatroid99 Dumping <i>an entire section of memory</i> might well not be possible, but it's far easier to save and load the memory representation of an integer, or even a variable-length list of integers, than to convert it into an equivalent text representation. Most binary file formats don't have a formal "serialization scheme", just ad hoc instructions for how to pack and unpack a stream of bytes, as in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-doc/26fb6c06-4e5c-4778-ab4e-edbf26a545bb" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this documentation of part of the legacy Microsoft Word format</a>.</span>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There is a Flash game, <em>Castlevania: The Blood Way</em>, which is hard to find on the internet today. One problem with that game is that it uses external resources: it loads SWFs from a specific domain, including level SWFs (0 to around 11 levels).</p>
<p>I've the SWF: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link</a></p>
<p>But the game doesn't play anymore. I tested it in the Ruffle player a few months ago and it worked, but the game stopped working now. I believe that the external resources have expired. Note that it doesn't work in the Flash Player projector too anymore.</p>
<p>I used FFDec a few months ago and was able to manipulate these external resources, but I lost everything. For some reason, now that I go to FFDec, I don't have idea of what are the domains. For example, I see that FFDec shows this ActionScript 2 code:</p>
<pre><code>loadMovieNum("musics/introB.swf",1,"GET");
</code></pre>
<p>The problem is, which is the base path for this resource? I tried to search for, say, <code>musics/introB.swf</code> in archive.org and didn't find anything. Not sure if this kind of search works in archive.org though. Any idea of what I'm missing? Because I was able to see the full absolute path of the resources...</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There is a Flash game, <em>Castlevania: The Blood Way</em>, which is hard to find on the internet today. One problem with that game is that it uses external resources: it loads SWFs from a specific domain, including level SWFs (0 to around 11 levels).</p>
<p>I've the SWF: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link</a></p>
<p>But the game doesn't play anymore. I tested it in the Ruffle player a few months ago and it worked, but the game stopped working now. I believe that the external resources have expired. Note that it doesn't work in the Flash Player projector too anymore.</p>
<p>I used FFDec a few months ago and was able to manipulate these external resources, but I lost everything. For some reason, now that I go to FFDec, I don't have idea of what are the domains. For example, I see that FFDec shows this ActionScript 2 code:</p>
<pre><code>loadMovieNum("musics/introB.swf",1,"GET");
</code></pre>
<p>The problem is, which is the base path for this resource? I tried to search for, say, <code>musics/introB.swf</code> in archive.org and didn't find anything. Not sure if this kind of search works in archive.org though. Any idea of what I'm missing? Because I was able to see the full absolute path of the resources...</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There is a Flash game, <em>Castlevania: The Blood Way</em>, which is hard to find on the internet today. One problem with that game is that it uses external resources: it loads SWFs from a specific domain, including level SWFs (0 to around 11 levels).</p>
<p>I've the SWF: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link</a></p>
<p>But the game doesn't play anymore. I tested it in the Ruffle player a few months ago and it worked, but the game stopped working now. I believe that the external resources have expired. Note that it doesn't work in the Flash Player projector too anymore.</p>
<p>I used FFDec a few months ago and was able to manipulate these external resources, but I lost everything. For some reason, now that I go to FFDec, I don't have idea of what are the domains. For example, I see that FFDec shows this ActionScript 2 code:</p>
<pre><code>loadMovieNum("musics/introB.swf",1,"GET");
</code></pre>
<p>The problem is, which is the base path for this resource? I tried to search for, say, <code>musics/introB.swf</code> in archive.org and didn't find anything. Not sure if this kind of search works in archive.org though. Any idea of what I'm missing? Because I was able to see the full absolute path of the resources...</p>
</div>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

            });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer

<button aria-controls="" aria-pressed="false" class="js-saves-btn s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py4" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-post-id="401531" data-post-type-id="1" data-s-popover-auto-show="false" data-s-popover-placement="" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-user-privilege-for-post-click="0" id="saves-btn-401531" title="Save this question.">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="fc-theme-primary-500 js-saves-btn-selected d-none svg-icon iconBookmark" height="18" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18"><path d="M3 17V3c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14l-6-4-6 4Z"></path></svg>
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="js-saves-btn-unselected svg-icon iconBookmarkAlt" height="18" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18"><path d="m9 10.6 4 2.66V3H5v10.26l4-2.66ZM3 17V3c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14l-6-4-6 4Z"></path></svg>
</button>
<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401531/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As a Shadow Priest, one of the choice nodes available on my talent tree is between Dark Ascension and Void Eruption. It's annoying when I switch this node as I have to routinely re-add the related cooldown ability to my action bar when I switch between them.</p>
<p>Is there a way to have both spells operate via the same macro so I can just use that macro as opposed to continually, and annoyingly, switching the spell that's on my bar?</p>
</div>

</div>
<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401532/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>During the pre-patch, Blizzard <a href="https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/psa-new-macro-conditional-known/1399019" rel="nofollow noreferrer">released "known" and "noknown" conditionals</a>, which can easily be used for choice node spells. The syntax for the conditional is <code>[known:&lt;spellid&gt;]</code> or <code>[known:&lt;spellname&gt;]</code>. This will also function as expected with <code>#showtooltip</code>.</p>
<p>The macro should look something like:</p>
<pre><code>#showtooltip
/cast [known:Dark Ascension] Dark Ascension; Void Eruption
</code></pre>
<p>Since Dark Ascension and Void Eruption are mutually exclusive, there's no break in logic here. If you select the question mark icon as the macro's icon, it will also take the icon of whatever spell you currently have learned.</p>
<p>Notably, as a Shadow Priest, Void Eruption will turn into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform. You do not need to specify a cast of Void Bolt in your macro, as Void Eruption basically turns into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform and while you are in Voidform, pressing this macro's button will cast Void Bolt as ordinarily expected.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As a Shadow Priest, one of the choice nodes available on my talent tree is between Dark Ascension and Void Eruption. It's annoying when I switch this node as I have to routinely re-add the related cooldown ability to my action bar when I switch between them.</p>
<p>Is there a way to have both spells operate via the same macro so I can just use that macro as opposed to continually, and annoyingly, switching the spell that's on my bar?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401532/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>During the pre-patch, Blizzard <a href="https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/psa-new-macro-conditional-known/1399019" rel="nofollow noreferrer">released "known" and "noknown" conditionals</a>, which can easily be used for choice node spells. The syntax for the conditional is <code>[known:&lt;spellid&gt;]</code> or <code>[known:&lt;spellname&gt;]</code>. This will also function as expected with <code>#showtooltip</code>.</p>
<p>The macro should look something like:</p>
<pre><code>#showtooltip
/cast [known:Dark Ascension] Dark Ascension; Void Eruption
</code></pre>
<p>Since Dark Ascension and Void Eruption are mutually exclusive, there's no break in logic here. If you select the question mark icon as the macro's icon, it will also take the icon of whatever spell you currently have learned.</p>
<p>Notably, as a Shadow Priest, Void Eruption will turn into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform. You do not need to specify a cast of Void Bolt in your macro, as Void Eruption basically turns into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform and while you are in Voidform, pressing this macro's button will cast Void Bolt as ordinarily expected.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As a Shadow Priest, one of the choice nodes available on my talent tree is between Dark Ascension and Void Eruption. It's annoying when I switch this node as I have to routinely re-add the related cooldown ability to my action bar when I switch between them.</p>
<p>Is there a way to have both spells operate via the same macro so I can just use that macro as opposed to continually, and annoyingly, switching the spell that's on my bar?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401532/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>During the pre-patch, Blizzard <a href="https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/psa-new-macro-conditional-known/1399019" rel="nofollow noreferrer">released "known" and "noknown" conditionals</a>, which can easily be used for choice node spells. The syntax for the conditional is <code>[known:&lt;spellid&gt;]</code> or <code>[known:&lt;spellname&gt;]</code>. This will also function as expected with <code>#showtooltip</code>.</p>
<p>The macro should look something like:</p>
<pre><code>#showtooltip
/cast [known:Dark Ascension] Dark Ascension; Void Eruption
</code></pre>
<p>Since Dark Ascension and Void Eruption are mutually exclusive, there's no break in logic here. If you select the question mark icon as the macro's icon, it will also take the icon of whatever spell you currently have learned.</p>
<p>Notably, as a Shadow Priest, Void Eruption will turn into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform. You do not need to specify a cast of Void Bolt in your macro, as Void Eruption basically turns into Void Bolt while you are in Voidform and while you are in Voidform, pressing this macro's button will cast Void Bolt as ordinarily expected.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401538/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Year after year I have been the one to host a minecraft server for a few weeks when the new minecraft update comes so me and my buddies can have some nostalgia.</p>
<p>Every year I set up the server. In my router settings I set the port and double check the if the server's internal ip is still good. and done. Then I give my friends my external ip. And everything works fine.</p>
<p>But this year I can't figure out why. None of them can join. Everything is the same. The router and it's settings, the pc I run the server on.
I'm the only one who can join the server and only with it's internal IP. But not with external one.</p>
<p>I just can't figure it out. I looked around for posts on the subject but did not manage the solve the problem.</p>
<p><strong>What I have tried so far:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Disabling the Firewall</li>
<li>Resetting the Router</li>
<li>Checking if the port forwarded internal ip is the right one</li>
</ul>
<p>Please help!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401560/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You may have been put behind CG-NAT (Carrier Grade NAT) wich would explain your problem very well. The short answer for why is that we are running out of IPv4 addresses. If you want the long answer for why, then you can read more about it here:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://www.a10networks.com/glossary/what-is-carrier-grade-nat-cgn-cgnat/</a></li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-grade_NAT</a></li>
</ul>
<p>
You should be able to test this by having your friends connect to you with your IPv6 address instead, if it is activated. If that works, then you're surely behind CG-NAT. Most ISP's should have IPv6 activated by now. Also, if you have a old router, IPv6 might not be activated by default or even worse, not be supported at all.
<p>If above works, then you don't really need to do anything as long as you play modern games that support IPv6.</p>
</p>
<p>
But contact your ISP and ask them if they have done something, if you are behind CG-NAT.
If it turns out that this is the case, then you can ask them for a public IPv4 address wich is the "normal" way. Some ISP's let you change back for free while some charge you for it. Some ISP's don't even have that service.
</p>
<p>
Another solution is to set up a virtual LAN. There are a couple of different softwares that can be used for this. GameRanger is a popular one. Hamachi used to be very popular, but don't seem to be so anymore.
</p>
</div>
