<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<li class="comment js-comment" data-comment-id="563922" data-comment-owner-id="172377" data-comment-score="2" id="comment-563922">
<div class="js-comment-actions comment-actions">
<div class="comment-score js-comment-score js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="cool" title="number of 'useful comment' votes received">2</span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">
– <a class="comment-user" href="/users/172377/plagiatus" title="1,238 reputation">Plagiatus</a>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/nrlrA.png"/></a></p>
<p>The command on this command block is:<br/></p>
<pre><code> /execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>I have another command block that has the command:</p>
<pre><code>/execute if entity @a[x=-519.5,y=141.0,z=-258.5,dx=0,dy=0,dz=0] run bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar players @a
</code></pre>
<p>So when I go to the coordinates in that command, the bossbar should be visible. If I put the command:</p>
<pre><code>/bossbar set minecraft:protectorbar visible true
</code></pre>
<p>in myself it works, the command block is powered on, and the other command blocks all work too, so I don't know why this one wouldn't work.</p>

<span class="comment-copy">ahaaaaa - that might as well be why. If that other commandblock is working as intended, and you're testing with the BJONK_BJONK player, then the issue is probably that that commandblock runs first, teleporting the player away from that place and then the subsequent commandblocks cannot find a player there anymore. To ensure that commandblocks run in the expected order, use chain commandblocks (the green ones).</span>
